sentences.text: This Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed against the order in M.C.O.P.No.53 of 2005 on the file of the I Additional Sub Judge, Nagercoil.
The appellant is the third respondent.
The first respondent is the claimant.
Respondents 2 to 6 herein are the respondents 1,2,4 to 6 in the claim petition.

2.Brief substance of the claim petition is as follows:
On 07.08.2001, when the petitioner was travelling in a jeep bearing registration number TN 74 Z 7832, driven by the fifth respondent in a slow and cautious manner,
n e a r J o t h i p u r a m , G R T P o l y t e c h n i c C o l l e g e , t h e s e c o n d https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis respondent drove the lorry bearing registration number KL 01 C 7551 in a rash and negligent manner, overtaking a government bus bearing registration number TN 45 N 1520, dashed against the jeep.
The petitioner and others sustained injuries.
One Peenish and Muthiah @ Nithiyan, died on the spot.
All the injured were taken to Tirunelveli Government Hospital.
Later, the petitioner was taken to Tirunelveli Devi Hospital and he took treatment from 07.08.2001 till 21.08.2001 as inpatient.
Subsequently, the petitioner took treatment as out patient.
The petitioner sustained permanent disability.
He was not able to walk, study or do any work.
The petitioner claimed a sum of Rs.8,00,000/- as compensation.

3.Brief substance of the counter filed by the third respondent is as follows:
It was the fifth respondent who drove the jeep in a rash and negligent manner, at the same time, another lorry that came from the same direction, dashed against the jeep and the jeep dashed against the bus that came from the opposite direction.
The lorry driver drove the vehicle in a slow speed.
Since the accident has taken place within a fraction of second, the lorry driver could not stop the vehicle.
The accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis driving of the fifth respondent, the unknown lorry driver and the bus driver.
The third respondent is no way connected with the accident.

Without proper investigation,
charge sheet was filed against the sixth respondent.
The real culprit has escaped from the clutches of law.
The petitioner has to prove his age, profession and income.
The accident has happened only due to the unknown lorry driver and the fifth New India Assurance Company Limited vs M.Rajesh ...

The petitioner claimed compensation only from the respondents 1 to 3 and not from the respondents 4 to 6.
The age, income are to be proved.

https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 5.Two witnesses were examined and ten documents were marked on the side of the petitioner.
One witness was examined and two documents were marked on the side of the respondents.

The Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.1,30,750/- as compensation to be paid by the respondents 1 to 3.
6.Against
the award
, the third respondent herein has filed this appeal on the following grounds:
The Tribunal failed to consider that the cause of the accident was the hitting by a unknown lorry from behind the jeep.

In the FIR, it is clearly stated that an unknown lorry hit the jeep from behind due to which the driver of the jeep lost the balance and the jeep dashed against the bus that came from the opposite direction.
The jeep was dragged further and it dashed against the lorry bearing registration number KL 01 C 7551 which came behind the bus.
The FIR has to be taken into consideration as a whole.
From Ex.R1, it is clear that the rear side of the jeep was damaged which prove that the jeep was hit by some other vehicle from behind.
The charge sheet filed by the police was completely contrary to the statement in the FIR and contrary to the statement recorded under Section 161(3) of Cr.P.C.
The Tribunal has failed to consider https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis that the criminal Court records were not binding on the Tribunal.
The permit for the lorry expired on 07.06.2001.
The appellant is not liable to indemnify the injured.

The Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities,
Rs.21,000/- towards loss of income, which are all excessive.
The entire award is excessive.
7.On the side of the appellant it is stated that it was an unidentified lorry that hit the jeep from behind which leads to a series of accidents.
The jeep dashed against the bus then dashed against the lorry that came behind the bus.
The Tribunal fixed the entire negligence on the lorry that came f behind the bus.

8.On the side of the claimant it is stated that totally two vehicles involved in the occurrence.
The first respondent is the owner of the lorry, the second respondent is the driver of the lorry, the third respondent is the insurer https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis of the lorry.
Respondents 4 and 5 are owner of the jeep and the sixth respondent is the insurance company.
9. On the side of the respondent it is stated that an unknown lorry hit from the back side of the jeep.

Thereby the jeep dashed against the opposite bus and that D.W.1 was not an eye witness and that the private investigation report was marked as Ex.R1 and that the appellant/ third respondent has failed to prove that the occurrence has happened only due to the rash and negligence of the fifth respondent.
10. On the side of the appellant, a judgment of this Court made in C.M.ANo.1147 of 2011, dated 24.11.2017 is cited.
P.W.1 has deposed that it was the second respondent who drove the lorry in a rash and negligent manner and he dashed against the jeep.
A private investigator appointed by the third respondent filed his report which was marked as Ex.R1.

Policy copy was marked as Ex.R2.
11.
After investigation, charge sheet was filed.
The second respondent has admitted his guilty and he has paid the fine in M.C.O.P.No.37 of 2002 and https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis the copy of the judgment was marked as Ex.P8.
The private investigation office appointed by the third respondent was not examined as a witness.
In the above circumstances, Ex.R1 cannot be taken into consideration, especially, when the private investigation officer was not examined as a witness.
12. R.W.1 was an official from the insurance company.

Even in the private investigation report,
Ex.R1, it is stated that the accident has happened due to the negligence of the second respondent.
The appellant failed to prove that the accident has occurred only due to the unidentified lorry.
Hence it is decided that the accident has happened only due to the rash and negligent driving of the third respondent / driver of the lorry.
13. On the side of the appellant, it is stated that there was no permit for the lorry to ply in Tamilnadu.
The permit expired on 07.06.2001 itself.
It is seen that the permit for the lorry was not valid at the date of accident.
From the evidence of R.W.2, it is clear that the lorry was registered in Kerala and the permit to use the lorry in Tamilnadu, expired on 02.06.2001 itself.
It is decided that the policy conditions were violated.

Hence the insurance https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis company is entitled to recover the compensation amount with interest and cost from the second respondent /
owner of the lorry.
14. On the side of the appellant it is stated that the Tribunal has awarded Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities, Rs.21,000/- towards loss of income which are all excessive.
The Doctor who gave treatment to the claimant was examined as P.W.2.
He has deposed that the claimant was having head injury and that there was fracture on the lower jaw bone.

sentences.text:
The discharge summary was marked on Ex.P9.
15.
It is seen that the claimants took treatment as inpatient from 07.08.2001 from 21.08.2001.
The Tribunal fixed the monthly income as Rs. 3600/- and for a period of six months, the Tribunal has awarded Rs.21,000/- as temporary loss of income.
The Tribunal has awarded Rs.5000/- towards transport expenses, Rs.7,000/- towards extra nourishment.
Rs.47,750/- towards medical expenses which are all reasonable.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis 16
. The Tribunal has awarded Rs.30,000/- towards pain and sufferings, Rs.20,000/- towards loss of amenities which are all excessive.
Considering the nature of the injury, it is decided that the petitioner is entitled to Rs. 20,000/- towards pain and sufferings.
The petitioner is not entitled to any amount towards loss of amenities.
Hence, the compensation is calculated as below.

Loss of income - Rs. 21,000/-
 Transport expenses - Rs. 5,000/-
 Extra nourishment - Rs. 7,000/-
 Medical expenses - Rs. 47,750/-
In the above circumstances, this Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is partly allowed.
No costs.

(i) The quantum of compensation awarded by the Tribunal is reduced from Rs.1,30,750/- to Rs. 1,00,750/- (Rupees One Lakh and Seven Fifty only) which shall carry interest at the rate of 7.5% per annum.

(ii) The appellant is directed to deposit the entire compensation of Rs.
1,00,750/- (if not already deposited) together with interest at the rate of 7.5%
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis per annum from the date of claim petition till the date of deposit with cost to the credit of in M.C.O.P.No.53 of 2005 on the file of the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal / I Additional Sub Court, Nagercoil, within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a copy of this order and the appellant permitted to recover the same from the owner of the vehicle.
(iii) On such deposit being made by the appellant herein, the first respondent / claimant is permitted to withdraw the entire award amount of Rs. 1,00,750/- (Rupees One Lakh and Seven Fifty only) with proportionate interest and cost.
The claimant is not entitled to interest for the default period, if there is any.
